turns.question: How are route parameters like :name captured during tree matching?
turns.text:
I still don't have a project loaded to inspect, so I can't point you to actual code for this. Route-parameter capture during tree/trie-based matching works roughly the same way across most routers (Express-style, `path-to-regexp`, httprouter, Gin, Echo, etc.):

- The router builds a tree where each path segment is a node — static segments (`/users`), parameter segments (`:name`), and wildcard segments (`*`).
- Parameter nodes are typically stored separately from static children (often checked after exact static matches, so static routes take priority over dynamic ones at the same depth).
- While walking the request path segment-by-segment, when the matcher hits a node marked as a parameter node, it captures the actual segment value from the URL and stores it (often keyed by the parameter name, e.g. `name`) in a params map/object, then continues descending.
- At the end of the path, if a matching leaf node (a registered route) is reached, the accumulated params are attached to the request/context object.

If you want a precise answer instead of the general pattern, share the repo or file (e.g., the router implementation) and I'll trace the actual matching code.
